domain_entities.name: DemoAccount
domain_entities.purpose: The idempotent development seed dataset: one manager, one employee, the leave types and policies the balance logic needs, a current-period balance for each, and two or three leave requests in different lifecycle states. Exists only in the development environment; never part of migrate.

domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: A person who can authenticate and request leave. The seed mints passwordHash via the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies with, so the demo account can log in.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: A single leave application. The seed creates requests in different states (e.g. SUBMITTED and APPROVED) so list and detail pages have data.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: One balance row per (employee, leave type, accrual period). The seed creates a balance for the current accrual period for each seeded employee, with counters consistent with the seeded requests.

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: The entitlement and accrual rules the balance logic needs. The seed creates an ACTIVE policy per seeded leave type.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Static catalog of leave types referenced by policies, balances, and requests. The seed creates the leave types the balance logic needs.

business_rules: Seed idempotency: a seeded row is identified by the composite key (employee, leave type, start date); if that key already exists the seed skips the row rather than duplicating or deleting it. This holds for every seeded entity that has such a natural key (leave requests, leave balances), and the seed must never delete or truncate existing data. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever development seed idempotency appears, not only here]

Leave balance counters must be consistent with the seeded requests: a SUBMITTED request's requestedDays appear in pendingDays, an APPROVED request's requestedDays appear in usedDays, and a DRAFT/REJECTED/CANCELLED request reserves nothing. This mirrors the canonical reservation lifecycle (submit increments pendingDays; approve decrements pendingDays and increments usedDays). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance counter consistency appears, not only here]

The seed is development data only and must never run as part of migrate. It is wired into the development environment of knexfile.js and invoked explicitly via a dedicated seed command, never by migrate:latest. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever development seed lifecycle appears, not only here]

requestedDays = endDate - startDate + 1 (inclusive calendar days, whole-day UTC, no weekend/holiday exclusion) is the single canonical day-count derivation. The seed must derive each seeded request's requestedDays via the shared requestedDays helper, never a hand-written count. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever requestedDays day-count derivation appears, not only here]

All seeded dates (hireDate, periodStart/periodEnd, request startDate/endDate, policy effectiveFrom/effectiveTo) follow the existing UTC date discipline: whole-day UTC instants derived via startOfUtcDay/periodContaining, never local-time or timezone-dependent values. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever seed UTC date discipline appears, not only here]

The demo account's passwordHash must be minted by the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies with (bcrypt.hashSync with the same cost factor), so POST /auth/login succeeds for the documented demo credentials. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever demo credential hashing appears, not only here]
domain_notes: Domain slice for the "runnable end to end" feature. No new lifecycle states are introduced — the seed reuses the existing canonical states: Employee ACTIVE|TERMINATED|ON_LEAVE; LeaveRequest DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED|CANCELLED; LeaveBalance OPEN|CLOSED; LeavePolicy DRAFT|ACTIVE|SUPERSEDED; LeaveType static (no lifecycle). The seed's leave requests must span at least two distinct LeaveStatus values (e.g. SUBMITTED and APPROVED) so list/detail pages render; the balance counters must reflect those states (SUBMITTED→pendingDays, APPROVED→usedDays). The seed is a development-only dataset (never part of migrate) and is idempotent on the composite key (employee, leave type, start date). All seeded dates follow the existing UTC discipline via startOfUtcDay/periodContaining, and requestedDays is derived only via the shared requestedDays helper. The demo passwordHash is minted with the same bcrypt call the auth service verifies. One open question remains: whether demo credentials are hardcoded literals or env-driven with defaults.

open_questions.question: Should the demo account credentials (email/password) be hardcoded in the seed or sourced from environment variables with documented defaults?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether the README documents fixed literal credentials or env-driven ones, and whether the seed violates the no-hardcoded-secrets constraint. The smoke.js precedent uses process.env with a default, but a demo account is intentionally non-secret.
candidate_options: Hardcode literal demo email/password in the seed and README (simplest, dev-only)
Source from env vars (e.g. DEMO_EMAIL/DEMO_PASSWORD) with documented defaults, matching smoke.js
Hardcode email but derive password from env with a default
